summary: Prefetch ripple and affinity imprint causing gradual dedicated throughput erosion in us-east pool
description:
Issue summary:
Customer AcmePay reports a gradual (~20% p50 throughput) degradation in their dedicated GPU pool in us-east starting 2026-02-10 10:15 UTC. Performance decline is steady (not a sharp outage) and correlates with an increase in small, long-lived streaming sessions from one tenant.

Impact:
- Customer-facing endpoints see ~15-25% lower successful inference throughput for batched routes during midday traffic window.
- P50 latency increased modestly (10-30%), p95 drifted to higher percentiles.
- No full 5xx outage; requests queued longer and some batches serialized, causing client backpressure.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-us-east-42 (gpu family: A100-80GB mix)
- Platform: prod (us-east)
- Affected routes: /v1/generate-batched (high-concurrency short-streams), /v1/stream (long-lived low-cpu streams)

Steps to reproduce / observed behavior:
1) Tail customer traffic for AcmePay between 10:00-12:00 UTC; steady mix of short and long streams.
2) Observe gradual drop in completed batched jobs/sec on dp-us-east-42.
3) Correlate with increased number of in-flight long context streams from tenant T-ACME-47.
4) Check scheduler logs: elevated prefetch lease renewals and contiguous affinity placements to a subset of GPUs despite autoscaler being healthy.

Logs / metrics (key findings):
- Serving runtime shows periodic KV-cache growth and prefetch loops: prefetch_rate spike ~2.3x at 10:12 UTC.
- GPU allocation logs: several lease rebinds to the same GPU stripe (affinity imprint) without rebalancing for >8 minutes.
- Autoscaler metrics: CPU/GPU utilization normal, no new nodes requested; allocation fairness score dropped ~30%.
- Scheduler queue depth: steady increase in per-slot pending batches; observed slot serialization for small streams.
- No driver crashes; no kernel errors in dmesg.

Initial hypothesis:
- A combination of aggressive KV prefetching from the long-lived streaming tenant plus scheduler affinity decisioning created an "affinity imprint" where repeated prefetches keep KV/cache pinned to a subset of GPU slots. That reduces effective batching capacity (slot fragmentation) and causes serialization of short batched routes (throughput erosion).

Investigation notes so far:
- Reproduced local workload with mixed small streams and long streams; when prefetch enabled and affinity sticky, observed similar slot serialization.
- Temporary mitigation: restarting the serving sidecar for T-ACME-47 freed pinned KV entries and restored throughput to baseline (~within 5 minutes).
- Kernel-level profiling suggests I/O waits on NVMe persisted KV shards during prefetch bursts; correlated with increased pcie latency in NVLink lanes.
- Scheduler team traced policy logs showing multiple affinity placements requested by the same tenant due to repeated reconnects, which the scheduler treats as preferred affinity (to reduce cold-kv misses).

Immediate mitigations attempted:
- Applied temporary affinity relaxation policy for dp-us-east-42 (trial window) — improved distribution of new streams across GPUs.
- Asked customer (AcmePay) to reduce their prefetch window for long streams as an experiment; they coordinated a throttled deployment and reported partial improvement.

Next steps / recommended actions:
- Short-term (0-24h): roll out affinity relaxation to 2 additional pools and monitor. Add a platform-side circuit breaker to limit prefetch concurrency per tenant.
- Medium-term (1-2 weeks): implement KV prefetch backpressure (server-side) and prefer balanced rebinds when prefetch counts exceed threshold.
- Long-term: scheduler heuristic change to avoid imprinting affinity for repeated short-lived reconnects; add telemetry to detect affinity imprint patterns and auto-relax.

Customer-facing notes for support reply:
- We acknowledge throughput degradation and have a temporary mitigation in place (affinity relaxation) that should reduce slot serialization. We recommend AcmePay temporarily reduce prefetch window while we validate the platform mitigation.

Postmortem / follow-ups:
- Owner: Diego Alvarez (runtime/scheduler) to lead root-cause and rollout the prefetch breaker.
- Follow-up ticket for platform / scheduler changes: INT-451900 (TBD).
